I or T: › [ I or T ] If something that has air or gas inside it deflates, or is deflated, it becomes smaller because it loses the air or gas.

T often passive: › [ T often passive ] to cause something to become weaker
› [ T often passive ] to make someone lose confidence or feel less important

T: › [ T ] to reduce the supply of money in an economy
使貨幣緊縮，使通貨緊縮

example: to deflate a balloon/tyre
給氣球／輪胎放氣
The party's ambitions have been deflated by the two recent by-election defeats.
最近的兩次補選失利使該黨的雄心受到了不小打擊。
They were totally deflated by losing the game.
他們輸掉比賽後徹底喪失了信心。

NONE: › feeling less confident and positive than before
灰心的，氣餒的

example: Her criticism left me feeling a bit deflated.
她的批評使我感到有點洩氣。

U: › the action of making something smaller by removing the air from inside it; the fact of becoming smaller in this way
› the situation in which something becomes weaker, or something or someone becomes less confident than before
› a reduction of the supply of money in an economy, and therefore a reduction of economic activity, that is often part of an intentional government plan to reduce prices

example: The rate of deflation of the balloon depends on the kind of material from which it is made.
氣球的漏氣程度取決於生產氣球的材料類型。
a feeling of deflation after the party
派對後的失落感
Compare
inflation
There has been a deflation in/of property values.
房地產出現了貶值。

NONE: › to (cause to) change direction, or to prevent something from being directed at you
（使）轉向，（使）偏斜

example: The ball deflected off my shoulder, straight into the goal.
球打在我的肩膀上反彈進了球門。
The crowd cheered as the goalkeeper deflected the shot.
當守門員把球擋出去的時候人們歡呼了起來。
He deflected the ball away from the goal.
他把球擋出了球門。
The prime minister deflected mounting criticism today by announcing tax cuts.
今天首相宣佈減稅，從而平息了越來越多的批評聲音。

NONE: › a change of direction, or the act of preventing something being directed at you
突然轉向；偏移，偏離

example: The second goal was from a deflection off the Liverpool captain.
第二個進球是從利物浦隊隊長的身上彈進去的。
The journalists were frustrated by her constant deflection of their questions.
她對問題一直避而不答，令記者們非常懊惱。

NONE: › to have sex with a woman who has never had sex before
使（女子）失去貞操；與（處女）發生性行為；姦汙（處女）
› to remove the mist (= thin layer of water drops) from the window of a car, usually by blowing air over it
（通常以吹風的方式）除去（汽車玻璃）上的霧氣
› a device that removes mist (= a thin layer of water drops) from a car window, usually by blowing air on it
（汽車玻璃）除霧器

example: Compare
defroster

NONE: › a chemical that is used to make the leaves drop off plants
落葉劑，枯葉劑
› to make the leaves drop off a plant, especially by using strong chemicals
（尤指使用強效化學品）使落葉，使凋零
› the cutting down of trees in a large area, or the destruction of forests by people
大面積砍伐森林；人為毀林

example: Deforestation is destroying large areas of tropical rain forest.
濫伐森林毀掉了大面積的熱帶雨林。

T: › [ T ] to spoil the usual and true shape of something
I: › [ I ] specialized chemistry If something deforms, its usual shape changes and becomes spoiled.

example: Age deforms the spine.
衰老會導致脊柱變形。

NONE: › with a shape that has not developed normally
畸形的；變形的
› the situation in which a part of the body has not developed in the normal way or with the normal shape
身體畸形，發育異常
› to make a computer organize its files and free space so that it can operate more quickly
（电脑）重新整理磁碟

example: Defragment your computer overnight.
讓你的電腦在夜間重新整理磁碟。

NONE: › to take something illegally from a person, company, etc., or to prevent someone from having something that is legally theirs by deceiving them
欺詐，詐騙

example: He was found guilty of defrauding the Internal Revenue Service.
他被判欺詐國內稅務署罪名成立。

NONE: › (especially of an organization) to pay the cost of something
（尤指由某組織）支付，承擔（費用）

example: The company will defray all your expenses, including car rental.
公司將承擔你的全部費用，包括租車費。

NONE: › to remove someone from your list of friends on a social networking website
在網路社交平臺上將某人從好友名單上去除

example: How do I check who has defriended me on Facebook?
怎麼才能查誰在臉書上把我從好友名單上去除了？

NONE: › to dismiss a priest (= remove him from his job), usually because of bad behaviour
免除（行為不端的牧師的）聖職
› to (cause to) become free of ice, or to (cause to) become no longer frozen
除霜；（使）溶化，（使）解凍

雞肉在煮食前要徹底解凍。

讓雞肉自行解凍。

NONE: › a device that removes frost (= a thin layer of ice) from a car window, usually by blowing warm air on it
（汽車玻璃）除霧器

example: Compare

NONE: › skilful, clever, or quick
熟練的；巧妙的；靈巧的

她巧妙地回答了記者的提問。

NONE: › no longer existing, living, or working correctly
不復存在的；死亡的；失靈的

NONE: › to stop providing the money to pay for something
停止支付；停止為…提供資金

example: She opposes any proposal to defund US troops.

T: › to prevent a bomb from exploding
› to make a difficult or dangerous situation calmer by reducing or removing its cause

example: Bomb disposal experts have defused a 110-pound bomb at a subway station this afternoon.
今天下午，排彈專家在一個地下鐵車站拆除了一枚110磅的炸彈。

NONE: C2 to refuse to obey a person, decision, law, situation, etc.
對抗；違抗；反抗
C2 to be extreme or very strange and therefore impossible to believe, describe, or explain
（因過於極端或奇特而）讓人無法相信／描述／解釋
› to tell someone to do something that you think will be impossible
激，惹；向…挑戰；

example: It is rare to see children openly defying their teachers.
很少看見孩子公然跟老師作對。
